applies_to: The German author-date convention: 'und' rather than 'and', 'u. a.' rather than 'et al.', 'vgl.'/'siehe' lead-ins, 'o. J.' for an undated work, 'S.' for a page locator.

cases.note: The plain German case. Present because the project deploys in German and an English-only detector would silently halve its recall there, with no error anywhere.
'und' has to join an author run exactly as 'and' does, or a two-author German citation loses its second author.
cases.text: Eine Replikation bestätigt dies (Müller und Schmidt, 2021).

cases.note: 'u. a.' is the German 'et al.', including the space inside the abbreviation that a typesetter may or may not have set.
cases.text: Der Effekt zeigt sich über Stichproben hinweg (Müller u. a., 2019).

cases.note: 'vgl.' is the most common German lead-in and appears inside the parentheses, where it would otherwise be read as the first word of the author name.
cases.text: Ein ähnliches Muster ist bekannt (vgl. Schmidt, 2021).

cases.note: A German group, mixing the 'u. a.' and 'und' forms, to check the split is on the semicolon rather than on any comma.
cases.text: Mehrere Arbeiten kommen zum selben Schluss (Müller u. a., 2019; Weber und Braun, 2021).

cases.note: German narrative position. The verb follows the parenthesised year, so nothing in the sentence marks the citation except the name-then-year shape.
cases.text: Müller und Schmidt (2021) berichten einen kleineren Effekt.

cases.note: 'o. J.' is the German 'n.d.'. It reaches this module from signals.py, which is where the bibliography path already reads it.
cases.text: Die Empfehlung gilt weiterhin (Müller, o. J.).

cases.note: 'S. 15' is a page locator, not an initial. The locator cue requires a following digit precisely so that '(S. Fischer, 2020)' keeps its author.
cases.text: Das Verfahren wird dort beschrieben (Müller, 2019, S. 15).

cases.note: The counterpart of the case above: 'S.' followed by a surname is a disambiguating initial and must not truncate the chunk.
cases.text: Eine frühere Fassung stammt von anderer Stelle (S. Fischer, 2020).

cases.note: A German month plus a year satisfies every structural test for a one-word surname plus a year. Only the month vocabulary separates them.
cases.text: Die Erhebung lief bis (Oktober 2021) und wurde dann beendet.
